    Deduplicate validation results by keeping the best candidate per reference

    deduplicate_references.Rd

    Reduces a table of validation results (typically produced by validate_references, which may contain several rows - several OpenAlex candidates - per reference) to a single row per reference, keeping for each group (source_file, ref_n) the candidate with the highest overall score (score_global).

    Usage

    deduplicate_references(data, verbose = TRUE)

    Arguments

    data

    data.frame or tibble. Validation results to deduplicate, which must contain the columns source_file, ref_n and score_global (structure typically produced by validate_references).

    verbose

    logical. If TRUE (default), displays a summary of the matching statuses (match_status) of the deduplicated table, in the same format as displayed at the end of the execution of validate_references.

    Value

    An object of the same type as data (data.frame or tibble), containing a single row per unique pair (source_file, ref_n) - the one with the highest score_global within that group - and preserving the order of the rows of the input table.

    Details

    Rows are grouped by the combination of the columns source_file and ref_n, which uniquely identifies each original bibliographic reference (the same reference may appear on several rows if several OpenAlex candidates were retained during validation).

    Score tie: in case of a tie in the maximum overall score within the same group, the first row encountered in the order of the input table is kept.

    The row order of the input table is preserved in the result: only the rows not retained are removed.

    See also

    validate_references for producing the multi-candidate results table expected as input.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
refs <- parse_references("my_file.tei.xml")
results <- validate_references(refs, verbose = TRUE)

# Keep only the best candidate per reference
unique_results <- deduplicate_references(results, verbose = TRUE)
} # }
